author: Chris Busch
releaseNotes:
2.4.3 - Findings from a review of the WaterGuru Integration that feeds this app. (1) WaterGuru's maintenance steps (replacing the cassette, the battery, calibration) are no longer passed through as dose advice. WaterGuru's doseAdvice covers every alert, so "Follow these steps to replace cassette" became the tile's recommendation and turned it RED. The cassette line now says "replace soon" or "replace now" when WaterGuru wants a new cassette. (2) The cassette line shows days left instead of "N tests left". CassetteChecksLeft counts test pads, and a C5 uses 6 of them per sample day, so 24 meant 4 days. The days come from the WaterGuru driver's cassetteDaysLeft when it has one and it is current, otherwise from WaterGuru's own text such as "4 days left". (3) The free-chlorine history behind the algae runway is recorded 20 seconds after a new sample arrives. WaterGuru sends the sample time before the chlorine reading, so the history mostly stored the previous sample's free chlorine, matched each dose to the wrong day and measured about twice the real daily loss, which made the runway about half as long as it should be. Readings stored before 2.4.3 are not used for the measured loss, so the runway shows an estimate until two new samples are in. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.4.2 - Follow-ups to 2.4.1. (1) A stop with nothing open (the STOP button on an idle app, a save, a run the app did not start) is anchored to its own request: a cached "off" no longer confirms it before the plug has answered. It says "stop requested" until a fresh OFF arrives, keeps its retries and cutoff, holds back a new dose meanwhile, and a late OFF still produces the final "stopped" notice. (2) An unchanged ON report (a profiler refresh answering a stuck relay) during a stop already in progress no longer restarts the stop, so the retry count is not reset and the EMERGENCY escalation and the cutoff run their course instead of an OFF every few seconds. (3) Saving the app rebuilds its jobs before stopping the pump, so a run the app is not tracking keeps its retries and cutoff; removing the app sends OFF once and says plainly that nothing will retry. (4) An emergency cutoff that is overdue runs at once instead of being pushed a whole window later. (5) The EMERGENCY notices wait a few seconds for the plug's OFF answer, like the stop notice; commands and re-arming are unchanged. (6) The running power watch stops once an OFF has been requested, so a stop can no longer latch a false power-loss fault. (7) The emergency cutoff latches the start fault when it stops an attempt that was never confirmed. (8) The tile publishes the dose record as forced events at confirmation and at a correction, so a dose with the same volume as the previous one, or a corrected volume under the unchanged lastDoseEpochMs, still reaches an external historian; a numeric attribute the app no longer knows (tank not initialised, FC or target missing, tank runway still learning) now reads -1 instead of keeping its last value. (9) Tank corrections for any install: adjust the tank estimate by a signed amount, and void a recorded dose that never ran (it leaves the dose history, its volume returns to the tank, the last-dose record is cleared only if it is that dose, and the tile republishes it as 0 mL). Neither touches the pump or today's dose total. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.4.1 - Fixes from the independent review of 2.4.0, built on platform behaviour measured on a live C8: a report whose value did not change arrives as an event with a fresh date but never re-dates the device's stored state. (1) An OFF report accepted by its event date is remembered, so a plug that was already off can still prove it: a fault after a lost ON can be acknowledged again instead of refusing forever, and a refusal with nothing open now says to press STOP for a fresh OFF report. (2) A confirmed run's power freshness uses the receipt time of the latest power report, so a steady reading no longer aborts a healthy run as power LOST. (3) A stop waits a few seconds for the plug's OFF report before saying anything; "stop requested ... Retrying" is sent only if the OFF is still unconfirmed. Retries and the independent cutoff are unchanged. (4) A run is booked from its ON report to its OFF report: a late OFF debits the extra volume from the tank, adds it to today's total and latches a stop-overrun review fault when it lands more than 30 s after the planned stop; an early stop books the tank from the observed run while today's total keeps the planned reservation; an unconfirmed attempt that demonstrably ran is counted too, without becoming a start. A correction republishes lastDoseMl under the dose's original lastDoseEpochMs, so a historian that keys doses by that value overwrites the point instead of counting a second dose. (5) The measured free-chlorine loss adds the app's own doses back between samples, so daily dosing no longer hides the loss; it needs the pool volume and chlorine strength, and skips dosed intervals without them. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.4.0 - Truthful pump start confirmation. A returned on() command is no longer reported as "pump started". For a power-capable selected switch, a start is confirmed only by a fresh ON plus fresh measured power at or above a configurable minimum (default 3 W); a non-power switch is confirmed by a fresh ON with an explicit power/flow-unverified notice. Cached readings from before the ON request never confirm a new start, and missing, null or throwing readings fail closed. An unconfirmed start alerts once, is stopped through the existing OFF/cutoff safety path (kept armed until the switch fresh-reports off), and latches a fault that stays visible until an explicit operator acknowledgement that never energises the pump or bypasses sample/day limits. While a power-confirmed run is active, loss of power or stale power evidence over a grace period (default 30 s) aborts safely. The attempted sample, planned volume and daily cap are reserved BEFORE the ON command, so a failure cannot make another automatic dose eligible; lastDose telemetry and tank inventory are booked only after confirmation, and a later partial/unknown failure leaves the volume uncertain for review without an automatic refund or retry. Existing historical state, ledgers and telemetry are preserved. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.3.2 - Confirmed-stop notice fix. A dose whose OFF is reported late now sends the one final stopped notification once the switch positively reports off, instead of silently clearing the active dose and its verification. Duplicate or idle OFF events stay silent, and the early-stop notice is unchanged. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.3.1 - Stop-lifecycle safety fixes. A pump stop is only "stopped" once the switch positively reports off: a failed, ignored or unreadable OFF keeps the independent emergency cutoff armed and keeps retrying rather than cancelling protection and reporting success. Re-arming never postpones a cutoff that is already due sooner, and saving configuration recreates the cutoff job with the time remaining instead of leaving a stored deadline with no timer behind it. A confirmed off releases the dose on every path, including a late off event or the cutoff finding the relay already off, so a later dose is no longer blocked by "a dose is already running". A failed start goes through the same confirmed-OFF handling, so a relay that energised before the ON command errored keeps its dose record and its cutoff. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.3.0 - The tile now reports lastCalcEpochMs beside lastCalc, so an external historian (InfluxDB/Grafana) can timestamp a target snapshot at the moment it was calculated rather than at collection time, which can be hours earlier or days if a run is missed. The app also re-renders the tank inventory and tank-runway lines in the stored preview after a dose, so the human-readable detail can no longer describe a fuller tank than the numeric attributes report. Requires the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver 1.3.0.

2.2.0 - Publish numeric dose, tank, and FC telemetry on the companion tile device (lastDoseMl, lastDoseEpochMs, lastDoseRuntimeSeconds, tankCapacityMl, tankRemainingMl, tankPercent, tankRunwayDays, freeChlorine, targetFreeChlorine) so an external historian such as InfluxDB/Grafana can store actual pump-started doses and calculate durable usage totals.

2.1.9 - Match the WaterGuru driver's capitalized raw cassette-life attribute names so checks, days and percent render in the preview.

2.1.8 - Add the exact date/time beside sample age, show WaterGuru cassette checks/days remaining, and estimate chlorine-tank runway from recorded app-controlled dose volumes.

2.1.7 - Move the current FC/pH/CYA/TA/CH snapshot from the Source section into the top preview, immediately above its sample-age line.

2.1.6 - Remove the duplicate remaining-tank paragraph below the top preview; the preview itself retains the full/remaining line.

2.1.5 - Move the detailed preview to the top of the app page, repeat the remaining-tank estimate below it, and show the next measurement and guarded automatic-dosing times.

2.1.4 - Show full and remaining chlorine-tank amounts in every detailed preview, and regenerate the preview immediately after a refill.

2.1.3 - Add a one-AUTO-dose-per-day guard so extra/manual WaterGuru measurements cannot cause a second automatic dose that day.

2.1.2 - Restrict AUTO pump starts to a configurable daily time window so manual morning measurements can update history without dosing.

2.1.1 - Add one daily, user-selected WaterGuru refresh so an evening measurement is imported promptly instead of waiting for the integration's next interval poll.

2.1.0 - Track chlorine-tank inventory for common container sizes, warn at a configurable low level, and block doses larger than the estimate.

2.0.4 - Send PushOver notices for pump start/stop and arm an independent, configurable emergency cutoff for every pump start.

2.0.3 - Explicitly support a continuously running circulation pump when no Hubitat interlock switch exists; approval/auto dosing requires this confirmation or a live circulation-switch interlock.

2.0.2 - Concise PushOver summary follows each new daily WaterGuru sample; the scheduled time is a once-per-day fallback if the event is missed.

2.0.1 - Concise scheduled PushOver summary always reports the calculated chlorine amount and pump runtime, including a zero-dose result.

2.0.0 - Guarded liquid-chlorine pump automation: advisory, approval and automatic modes; 185 mL/min runtime conversion; freshness, pH, per-dose, daily-dose and runtime limits; duplicate-sample lock; circulation interlock; scheduled stop and emergency watchdog.

1.3.0 - Chlorine runway (algae forecast): estimate days until free chlorine drops below the algae-prevention floor (0.075 x CYA), learning your pool's daily FC loss from a rolling sample history (ignoring chlorine additions), with a cover-aware estimate until history builds up or a manual ppm/day override. Shown in the message, the tile detail, and the tile footer.

1.2.0 - Show the WaterGuru cassette type (C2/C5) — when the source device's WaterGuru Integration driver reports it (cassetteType/cassetteInfo) — in the notification/tile-detail header and as a line on the dashboard tile. Degrades silently on older drivers that don't expose it.

1.1.0 - At-a-glance features: each pool advisor can now maintain a dashboard tile device (a WaterGuru Dosing Tile device exposing status/recommendation/detail/tileHtml/lastCalc) and send an optional daily summary notification at a chosen time. Adds the WaterGuru Dosing Tile driver.

1.0.0 - Initial release. Parent/child: one advisor per WaterGuru pool. SLAM/CYA-aware free-chlorine dosing, pass-through of WaterGuru's own pH/TA/CH/CYA advice, generic fallback formulas, and single-message delivery to notification devices.
